0.headline: OPINION | Anthropic’s IPO and the changing ways retail investors participate in the AI market
0.heading: OPINION | Anthropic’s IPO and the changing ways retail investors participate in the AI market
0.intro: The IPO was a trendsetter and expanded retail opportunities to participate in the AI boom. Through ETFs and tokenised products, however, a wider cohort of retail investors across the world has jumped in. But risks need careful monitoring
0.body:
For much of the AI boom, only a relatively small group of investors had access to the biggest investment opportunities. Early funding rounds in companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic were largely reserved for venture capital firms, institutional investors, and wealthy individuals. By the time these companies became accessible to the wider market, much of their early growth had already taken place. 

Anthropic’s IPO expands the retail pathway

Anthropic’s IPO marks an important shift in this landscape. It is not just another technology company entering the public markets. It reflects how the opportunity to invest in artificial intelligence is gradually moving beyond private investment circles and becoming accessible to a wider set of investors. 

However, the way retail investors participate in this opportunity is changing. An IPO is only one route. Investors are increasingly finding exposure through public markets, investment funds, and products that hold stakes in private companies. 

The IPO is changing the access conversation 

One of the most important aspects of Anthropic’s public offering is the scale of capital being raised. This means the IPO is not simply an exit for early investors. A significant part of the capital raised is intended to support the company's next phase of growth. 

Retail participation has also become an important part of the IPO process, with a portion of the offering made available through brokerage platforms. But access does not necessarily mean equal opportunity. Retail allocations are limited, demand can exceed supply, and investors buying after listing may have to pay a market price significantly different from the IPO price. 

Institutional and early-stage investors have participated in the company's growth over several years. Retail investors entering at the IPO stage are evaluating the business at a much later point in its journey, when expectations around growth and valuation are already reflected in the price. 

Retail access is expanding beyond IPOs 

Retail investors are finding ways to participate in the AI boom without having to pick individual winners or wait for an IPO. AI-themed ETFs have grown rapidly, with assets reportedly rising from $10.3 billion to $64.9 billion in a year. Investors are also gaining exposure through semiconductor funds, broad market index funds and mutual funds that already hold stakes in private AI companies such as Anthropic. 

Some are seeking earlier exposure through private-market funds and tokenised or derivative products, while leveraged ETFs and options offer ways to take larger positions with less upfront capital. However, these routes come with different risks, including high fees, limited liquidity, leverage and, in some cases, no direct ownership in the underlying company. 

Access to AI investments is expanding, but it does not necessarily mean better diversification or lower risk. As investors look beyond IPOs, understanding what they actually own, how much they pay for access, and how easily they can exit becomes just as important as choosing the investment itself. 

What this means for Indian investors 

For Indian retail investors, access to global AI opportunities is also evolving. While the Anthropic IPO prospectus does not constitute an offer to the public in India, investors may explore overseas investment routes after listing, subject to applicable regulations and eligibility requirements. 

These include investing through the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), eligible GIFT City platforms, tokenized stocks, and Indian mutual funds with international exposure. Each route has different costs, investment limits, tax implications, and operational requirements. Investors should understand these before making a decision. 

The larger opportunity for Indian investors is that participation in the AI economy no longer has to depend on identifying one company at the right time. Exposure can come from across the value chain, including software, chips, cloud infrastructure, and other businesses supporting AI adoption. 

The next phase of AI investing 

Anthropic's IPO is part of a broader change in how investment opportunities are reaching retail investors. The boundary between private and public markets is becoming less rigid, and financial products are creating new ways to access businesses at different stages of growth. 

But wider access should not be confused with lower risk. Investors must evaluate the underlying business, understand the structure of the product, account for fees and liquidity, and ensure that the investment fits their financial goals.  

The real opportunity is not simply to get access to the next big AI company. It is to understand where value is being created across the AI ecosystem and participate in that growth through informed, well-planned investment decisions. 

&nbsp;

(Prateek Gupta, Head of Business, Mudrex.) 

Views are personal and do not represent the stand of this publication.

1.headline: Anthropic becomes one of the most-traded US stocks on Indian platforms on debut
1.heading: Anthropic becomes one of the most-traded US stocks on Indian platforms on debut
1.intro: The AI company's shares accounted for 11 percent of Vested's traded value on Thursday, while Anthropic made up 40 percent of international investments on INDmoney.
1.body:
Anthropic emerged as one of the most actively traded US stocks among Indian investors on November 19, accounting for 40 percent of international investments on INDmoney and 11 percent of the total traded value on Vested, according to the companies.

INDmoney and Vested are the two largest platforms for international investing for Indians through the GIFT City route.

On Thursday, Anthropic shares made a strong Nasdaq debut, opening at $111.5 apiece, a premium of 34 percent over their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83.

The opening price pushed the AI firm's valuation to approximately $2 trillion, following the world's largest-ever public share sale, surpassing Elon Musk's SpaceX listing.

On INDmoney, the average order value for Anthropic was also around twice the platform's average order value, it said.

On Vested, Anthropic accounted for around 11 percent of the total traded value and 9 percent of the total number of trades placed on the platform during Thursday's session. It emerged as the second most-traded stock by value, behind AMD and ahead of Nvidia.

However, the interest was concentrated in the initial hours of trading, with 84 percent of all Anthropic trades on Vested being placed within the first two hours of the stock beginning to trade.

Nearly 20 percent of all active traders on the platform during the session bought Anthropic shares, with the average buy order size at around $1,100, or roughly 10 shares.

Anthropic was also traded around seven times more than Nvidia on Vested during Thursday's session, indicating the intensity of investor interest in the newly listed AI company.

The strong first-day participation follows heightened interest among Indian investors ahead of the listing.

Investment platforms had reported a sharp increase in enquiries around the company, with some older global investing platforms seeing nearly three times the interest compared with the SpaceX listing.

The latest listing also comes at a time when large domestic brokers such as Groww, Upstox, Zerodha and Angel One have entered international stock investing through GIFT City, significantly widening access to US equities for Indian investors.

The first-day trading activity suggests that the interest in Anthropic translated into actual buying on platforms facilitating international investments.

"The first day measures demand, not value. The real test will come over the next few quarters: whether margins improve as compute costs fall, whether growth holds up against competition, and how the stock behaves when lock-ins expire," Naresh Biyani, founder and CEO of Capwise Financial Services.

He added that the strong debut reopens the window for large AI listings like OpenAI, though valuations could stay volatile.

The data does suggest that semiconductor companies like AMD and Nvidia continue to enjoy investor confidence, even as Anthropic attracted investor interest on day one.

2.headline: Crystal Crop Protection IPO booked 4x so far on Day 3; check latest GMP
2.heading: Crystal Crop Protection IPO booked 4x so far on Day 3; check latest GMP
2.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Crystal Crop Protection continued to witness strong investor interest on the last day of bidding, with the issue receiving 3.9 times subscription by 10:50 am on November 20, as per NSE data.
2.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Crystal Crop Protection continued to witness strong investor interest on the last day of bidding, with the issue receiving 3.9 times subscription by 10:50 am on November 20, as per NSE data.

The Rs 455.49-crore IPO received bids for 4,74,71,270 shares against 1,21,70,076 shares on offer. The non-institutional investors (NIIs) led the demand with a subscription of 5.76 percent, followed by retail investors with 4.04 percent subscription.

In the grey market, Crystal Crop's shares were commanding a premium of around 7 percent on the morning of November 20, according to data from InvestorGain.

Read Also: Ashton Kutcher backed Anthropic despite wife Mila Kunis’ disapproval: His $435 million bet is now worth $7 billion

The grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment towards an IPO ahead of its listing. However, it does not guarantee listing gains, and the premium can fluctuate depending on market conditions and demand for the issue.

The Rs 455.49-crore IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 354.77 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 37.03 lakh equity shares aggregating approximately Rs 100.71 crore.

While the proceeds from the fresh issue will go to the company, the OFS will allow promoter Ankur Aggarwal to offload part of his shareholding. The proceeds from the OFS will go to the selling shareholder.

Crystal Crop Protection plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue primarily to repay or prepay certain outstanding borrowings of the company and its material subsidiary, Saffire Crop Science.

A portion of the proceeds will also be utilised to support inorganic growth through acquisitions and other strategic initiatives, besides meeting general corporate purposes.

The lot size for the Crystal Crop Protection IPO is 55 equity shares, and investors can apply for shares in multiples of 55.

At the upper end of the IPO price band, retail investors will need a minimum investment of Rs 14,960 to apply for one lot of 55 shares, excluding applicable charges.

The issue has reserved 50 percent of the net offer for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 35 percent for retail individual investors and 15 percent for non-institutional investors (NIIs).

Check IPO News Here

The basis of allotment for the Crystal Crop Protection IPO is expected to be finalised on November 23. The initiation of refunds and credit of shares to successful applicants' demat accounts are scheduled for November 25.

The company's shares are tentatively scheduled to list on the BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on November 26.

About Crystal Crop Protection

Established in 1994, Crystal Crop Protection is an agricultural solutions company headquartered in New Delhi. Its business portfolio spans crop protection products, seeds and other agricultural solutions.

The company manufactures and markets a range of crop protection products, including herbicides, fungicides and insecticides. Its portfolio also includes natural crop solutions such as bio-protectants, bio-stimulants, liquid fertilisers, plant growth regulators and micronutrients.
